concepts.title: Square Identities (a + b) squared and (a - b) squared
concepts.definition: Area models of squares prove the two square identities for all values: (a + b) squared equals a squared + 2ab + b squared, and (a - b) squared equals a squared - 2ab + b squared; splitting numbers like 103 as 100 + 3 turns squaring into easy mental pieces.
concepts.formula: value = a * a + 2 * a * b + b * b
concepts.key_idea: Square the parts, double the cross: the identity works for every a and b.
question_patterns: use the identity to find 105 squared
expand (2x + 3y) squared using the standard identity
evaluate (a - b) squared for the given values
verify the identity with a diagram of areas
find the square of 98 using (100 - 2)
which identity expands the given expression

solution_steps.explain: Compute a squared and b squared.
The cross term 2ab completes the identity.

concepts.title: Difference of Squares Identity
concepts.definition: The product of a sum and the matching difference collapses to the difference of squares: (a + b)(a - b) equals a squared minus b squared - the shortcut behind computations like 51 times 49 equals 2500 minus 1.
concepts.key_idea: Sum times difference: middle terms cancel and only the squares survive.
concepts.textbook_ref: iemh104.txt sections on difference of squares identity
question_patterns: evaluate 51 x 49 using the difference of squares

which identity simplifies the given product
compute 102 x 98 by the identity and check

solution_steps.explain: The product is big square minus b squared.

concepts.title: Factorisation Using Identities
concepts.definition: Identities read backwards factorise expressions: a squared + 2ab + b squared collapses into (a + b) squared, a squared minus 2ab plus b squared into (a - b) squared, and a squared minus b squared into (a + b)(a - b).
concepts.key_idea: Match the pattern, name the a and b, and the brackets write themselves.
concepts.textbook_ref: iemh104.txt sections 4.6-4.7 (factorisation using identities, new identities)
question_patterns: factorise x squared + 10x + 25 using identities

solution_steps.explain: Compare the expression with the three standard identity forms.
The square terms reveal a and b.
The identity gives the factorisation directly; expand back to check.

concepts.title: Simplifying Rational Expressions
concepts.definition: A rational expression is a quotient of polynomials; factorising numerator and denominator and cancelling the common factors simplifies it, just as common factors cancel in ordinary fractions.
concepts.key_idea: Factorise both floors of the fraction, then cancel what is common.
question_patterns: simplify the given rational expression

solution_steps.explain: Use identities and common factors on both parts.
Delete the factors that appear on both sides.
Values that make the original denominator zero are excluded.
